title: Controls & accessibility
text: Controls & accessibility Use the Controls & Accessibility panel beside dispatch’s ready board. You can also reach it from the van and personal inventory. Preferences are saved separately for desktop, VR, and touch. Desktop: keep chase actions on keys Action Default Temporary cursor menu Hold Tab ; release to close the entire menu Keep menu open for reading I ; press again to close Draw reusable equipment 1 Draw equipped consumable 2 Stow personal item 3 Select reserve 1 / 2 4 / 5 Drop task cargo 6 Use drawn item Native Use action / Use button Collect or work Targeted world interaction / context action On the tested desktop client, Tab stops movement. This also happened in another world. Plan cursor interaction while stationary, preferably in the refuge. Shift+Tab may not open the menu while sprinting; release sprint first. I keeps a reading panel visible but does not unlock the mouse: hold Tab to click. The six numbered shortcuts work without Tab, including with Shift held. They can be rebound, and conflicting bindings are reported. Reserve selection swaps the chosen reserve into the equipped slot; it does not draw or consume it. Press 2 to draw, then make a fresh Use input. A saved Tab Hold / Stay open preference is available. VR: wrist or floating panel Select the wrist launcher to open the inventory and tap a slot. Choose either wrist and either equipment hand. A floating panel alternative has adjustable position and size for seated play and different avatar scales. Opening the default inventory does not freeze movement. Personal items follow the chosen hand. Cargo uses normal pickup controls, or the accessible Carry / Drop actions. If a native pickup occupies the equipment hand, stow or move it deliberately; personal equipment must not forcibly release it. Phone and tablet Use the screen’s INVENTORY , USE ITEM , and COLLECT / WORK buttons. The world-space lobby boards are also present, but the screen controls are the intended touch shortcut. Inside inventory, select equipment, consumables, or reserves; use the separate Use action to activate the selected item. The iPhone build has been tried by the creator. Final touch layout and ergonomics still need broader device testing. Preferences and practice Hold or toggle repair/rescue interactions. Accessible cargo carrying with the same reservation, penalty, delivery, and drop rules. Wrist/equipment handedness and floating panel placement/size. Desktop key rebinding with conflict feedback and reset defaults. Separate persisted control profiles for each input family. Optional inventory stick navigation, off by default : neutral deadzone 0.25, activation threshold 0.70, dwell 150 ms. Return to neutral before another step; selection requires confirmation. These settings control SpookCo actions, not VRChat’s native movement bindings. Use the free practice station to check your setup. Selecting or collecting an item never activates it automatically.

title: Equipment & field supplies
text: Equipment & field supplies Your inventory You have one reusable equipment slot , one equipped consumable , two reserve consumables , and one separate task-cargo slot . Duplicates are allowed; each occupies a slot. Purchases and scavenged supplies use the same three-slot pouch. Only one personal item is actively held at a time. Switching personal items does not discard cargo. Selecting a reserve swaps it with the equipped consumable. Collecting, selecting, and drawing do not automatically use an item; consuming one does not activate the next. Reusable equipment Unlocks use lifetime survival-point milestones. Points are not spent. Equipment Survival points Role Wind-up decoy 0 Place a distraction to pull the hunter’s investigation away. Instant camera 12 A close-range flash can stun the killer; cooldowns and post-stun immunity limit repeated use. EMF pager 40 Passive proximity information about the killer. Track shoes 100 Passive 10% movement bonus, within the shared bonus cap. Pager and shoes work without an active Use effect. Gear selection happens during shopping/loadout windows. Active gear has cooldowns; reconnecting or resetting must not refresh them. Cash consumables These prices and effects describe the current baseline and may be rebalanced. Supply Cash Effect Field ration 18 Restores one health when below your maximum. Sprint soda 16 Eight-second movement boost; total positive movement bonuses cap at 20%. Rescue flare 22 Rescues a nearby downed teammate within 12 metres. Needs a valid teammate. Repair tape 20 Applies progress to an eligible nearby repair. Needs a valid repair target. If the effect has no valid target, the request is rejected without spending the item. The shop guarantees a chosen supply, while field scavenging trades time and risk for a shared find. Shared field loot Each stop rolls supplies at distinct authored locations. They are global pickups : once one player successfully collects an item, nobody else can collect that spawn. A full pouch shows Pouch Full and leaves it available. Starting participants Shared items 1 1–2 2 1–3 4 2–4 8 3–7 12 4–9 16 6–12 The four cash consumables can appear, with equal initial weights and duplicates allowed. Solo stop rolls omit the teammate-focused rescue flare. Supplies are optional: a contract never requires finding one. A pickup goes into the equipped consumable slot if empty, otherwise the first empty reserve. It is stored without being drawn. Collecting supplies awards no XP or cash. Unclaimed supplies disappear when the stop ends; collected supplies stay in your session pouch. Joins, host changes, restarts, and trip resets do not reroll or replenish previously claimed supplies.

title: Dispatch FAQ
text: Dispatch FAQ Is this the finished game? No. This is a playable graybox under active development. Expect placeholder art and sound, changing balance, and unfinished edge cases. Spectator radar and AI diagnostics are development tools that may be removed. PC, Android/Quest, and iOS bundles have been built; broad device and multiplayer acceptance is still in progress. How many people can play? The implemented participant limit is 16 , and solo play is supported. Handling the creator/instance-creator overflow case of 18 people in an instance is accepted work but is not implemented yet. Do not rely on overflow admission for a playtest. Can I pass control of the game to someone else? Yes. Open Host , select a player, and offer Pass Host . They have 20 seconds to accept; the current host stays in control until acceptance. This transfers the game-host role, not VRChat’s instance ownership or master role. What if the host goes AFK? After five minutes without meaningful activity, another player can Claim Host . A visible/audible 20-second warning gives the host time to use Keep Hosting or resume meaningful input. If the host leaves, claiming becomes available immediately. Only one claim can be pending. The creator has tested Pass Host and AFK Claim Host in uploaded play. Less common cases such as claimant departure and simulation-owner suspension still need expanded testing. What else can the host do? Force Start the ready players, Stop After This Stop, Restart Current Stop, or Reset Trip. Restart/reset require hold confirmation and preserve legitimate rewards, purchases, and cached loot claims. Repeated resets are not a way to generate free supplies. Why did the round start without me? Force Start departs with players who are ready. Loading players and spectators are excluded from the ready denominator. You can opt in later under the joining rules . Why can’t I see the live field map? The map is for eligible spectators at dispatch. Joining the crew, being downed, or waiting to enter as a participant removes live tracking. A missing or delayed network snapshot displays a waiting/tracking-age message. Why does Tab stop me on desktop? That happened in the tested VRChat client, including another world. Use the direct keyboard shortcuts during movement. I can pin the menu for reading, but Tab is still needed for clicking. What makes a useful bug report? Tell the playtest organizer the platform, approximate time, number of players, area, killer, and what happened before the issue. Include whether you were host or spectator, a screenshot if useful, and the build being tested. Avoid posting raw client logs publicly; they can contain account or session details.

title: Your first shift
text: Your first shift Development build: art, balance, and features are still changing. Spectator radar and AI diagnostics are temporary development features, not promises for the finished game. 1. Get ready at dispatch Wait for your saved progress to finish loading. Choose Ready / Join to take part, or Watch / Withdraw to spectate. When everyone enrolled is ready, a five-second countdown starts. Becoming unready cancels an automatic countdown. The game host can Force Start with at least one ready player. Only players ready at departure join the initial crew. A solo player uses the same ready-up flow. Find Controls & Accessibility beside the ready board. Try the practice station before spending supplies; practice does not spend session purchases or award progression. 2. Read the contract A trip has three stops. Each begins with a 20-second briefing for the contract, shop, and loadout. The two areas alternate and each stop uses a different killer. These are current tuning values, not fixed release promises. 3. Head into the field The expedition lasts up to 150 seconds . Carry orange cargo cases back to the van and repair green equipment. Repairs retain progress when interrupted. Every required objective can be done alone without a purchased item or specific perk. Crew at stop start Cargo Repairs 1 2 1 2 3 1 3–4 5 2 5–8 8 3 9–12 12 4 13–16 16 5 Late joins never raise an active stop’s quota. Departures or withdrawals can lower requirements while preserving finished work. Downed players and teammates sheltering at the van still count. 4. Regroup and extract The covered campfire refuge beside the van is protected throughout the stop. Enter and leave freely. The current van body is a solid placeholder; use the covered exterior, not the van’s body as an entrance. Finishing the quota opens 30 seconds of extraction early. Running out of expedition time triggers emergency extraction instead. Get back before departure: it does not wait indefinitely for missing players. Transit takes 10 seconds and uses a fade/teleport instead of driving standing avatars around. Two completed contracts count as a successful shift; all three give the best report. Staying safe without participating does not earn activity rewards. If you go down You normally start with two health. A short immunity interval prevents immediate repeated hits. A downed player has a 12-second rescue window ; a teammate can perform a three-second rescue, or two seconds with Field Medic. If no able teammate remains, including solo play, the rescue wait is skipped. Otherwise, when the rescue window expires, an eight-second recovery returns you to the van. Dropped cargo can be recovered. Capture never removes banked XP or survival points. Second Wind allows a six-second field recovery on the first down of a stop. Joining a trip already in progress Use Ready / Join from dispatch. During an expedition you can opt in at the van. Arrivals during extraction or transit enter at the next briefing. Joining does not generate extra field supplies or increase the current quota. Continue with controls , equipment , and killer counterplay .

title: Progression & saving
text: Progression & saving The save system is implemented, but reconnect and multi-instance edge cases still need expanded uploaded testing. Do not treat a development build as a permanent economy guarantee. What stays with you Resource Purpose Intended lifetime XP Levels and perk-point capacity Permanent across visits Survival points Lifetime equipment milestones; never spent Permanent across visits Cash Buy consumables The live instance session Consumable pouch Purchased and scavenged supplies The live instance session Build and controls Perk/equipment choices and device preferences Saved across visits Rejoining the same live session is designed to restore cash, pouch contents, and relevant equipment state. A → B → A uses separate records while A remains live. Up to 128 recent sessions are retained. When everyone leaves, that session ends; a later fresh session begins with fresh cash and supplies. Wait for restoration before shopping or collecting. Accepted changes are saved during play, not just on departure. A sudden crash can lose the most recent cloud write. Capture does not remove banked XP or survival points. Levels and perk points Start at level 1 with 2 points . Gain one point every three levels, reaching 15 points at level 40 . Choose any combination of unique perks within your budget and respec freely during briefings. Perk Cost Current effect Spotter 1 Objective markers visible 50% farther away Courier 2 Removes the cargo movement penalty Mechanic 2 Repairs 25% faster Field Medic 2 Rescue interaction takes two seconds Scrapper 2 20% more objective cash Soft Soles 3 Movement hearing range reduced by 25% Adrenaline 3 Extraction movement bonus Quickdraw 3 Active equipment cooldowns reduced by 20% Hardhat 4 One extra maximum health Second Wind 4 Six-second field recovery on first down each stop Combined positive movement bonuses are capped at 20%. Perks support different roles; required tasks remain possible with the starter loadout. XP comes from objectives, bounded rescue participation, participated contract/extraction results, and trip results. Idle waiting and supply collection do not generate XP. The level curve totals 31,785 XP to level 40. A 20+ hour route to full capacity is a design target , not a measured result yet.

title: Know the threats
text: Know the threats One killer is active at a time. The creator has accepted the current AI as a working baseline, with more polish and balance work ahead. None of these descriptions guarantees an easy escape. Killer What it does What to try Groundskeeper Sight pursuit, remembered routes, and local searches Break sight, change route, and quietly leave its search area. Rattletrap Blind; investigates movement and task noise Walk when possible, time repairs, and use a decoy. Roadkill Telegraphs a fast, committed charge Dodge sideways and put solid cover between you and its line. Hitchhiker Uses concealed authored ambush positions Watch roadside silhouettes and change approach. Usher Warns before committing from its vision cone Get out of the cone or behind cover before the lock completes. Switchboard Pursues and marks work-site/route hazards Leave the marked area and switch sites. Your footsteps matter All killers hear movement in every direction, including behind cover. Running can be heard farther away than walking. Quiet, stationary players do not continuously give away a new movement position. Soft Soles reduces movement hearing ranges by 25%. This senses in-game movement and certain task events. It does not listen to microphone audio or voice chat. One corner is not a guaranteed escape Hunters can continue toward the last observed route, investigate sound, scan while moving, and check nearby paths. Current search budgets vary from 12 to 22 seconds and three to five search locations, depending on the killer. Search can finish when its point budget is exhausted. Break sight, change route, reduce noise, and use the protected refuge when needed. Sound gives the AI an investigation point; it is not treated as direct vision through a wall. Spectating the current build Choose Watch / Withdraw to remain at dispatch. The Live Field Map shows crew and killer tracking. In the current test build, a gold outline depicts vision and blue rings depict walking/running hearing; Rattletrap has hearing only. Tracking is for lobby spectators, not active or downed crew. Development feature: visible sensing radar and AI diagnostics may change or disappear from the final game. The map is a simplified horizontal view, not a guarantee of detection at every height or through every shape of cover.

title: SpookCo: Last Stop
text: The night shift has a survival clause. Take the company van into the dark. Recover cargo, patch up the equipment, and get everyone back to the campfire lantern before departure. Something out there heard you clock in. Three stops. One questionable employer. SpookCo: Last Stop is a cooperative horror world built around short expeditions and a dependable refuge. Play alone or bring a crew of up to 16. Finish the work, scavenge what you can, and decide when to make a run for the van. Clock in Ready up at dispatch, choose your equipment, and read the contract. A new stop brings a new job and a different hunter. Do the work Recover cargo and repair equipment. Field supplies are shared: whoever collects a pickup gets it. Running is faster, but it carries farther through the dark. Make it back The van’s covered campfire refuge stays safe. Complete the quota to open extraction early, or scramble aboard during emergency extraction. Departure has a deadline. A small world with a long night ahead Two prototype locations are playable: Camp Deadwood and Last Chance Service Station . Six killers have different hunting patterns, with sight, movement hearing, and searches that follow recent evidence. This is a playable development build , with placeholder environments, characters, and sound. The basic loop works; the next focus is game and environment design. Balance, visuals, and features will change. Spectator sensing radar and AI diagnostics are test tools and may be changed or removed before release. Your first shift Start with the quick-start guide , check your controls , or learn what to pack in the equipment guide . The site describes the current baseline; an older uploaded build may behave differently.
